label: Child widget by name
summary: The child element of the current interface widget that has the given name.
details: Going by its name and its use, it looks up a widget inside the current one by its name. Vanilla uses it in the bookmark screen to find the character selection button and start an animation on it (FindChild('bookmark_character_selection_button').TriggerAnimation(...)). The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the child widget to find.
fields.values: a widget name in quotes, for example 'bookmark_character_selection_button'

label: Number of child widgets
summary: How many child elements the interface widget has, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type directly; the ledger window uses it after FindChild to check whether its pinned grid holds anything (greater than 0), which fits the name.

label: Position in list
summary: The position of the widget's item in the list it was made from, as a whole number counted from 0.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla adds 1 to it to show the keyboard shortcut number of each event option (Alt + 1, Alt + 2 …) in the event window.

label: Widget name
summary: The name of the interface widget, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger's sort buttons: the widget's name is joined to a prefix such as sort_l_ and the result is looked up as a localization key, so each button shows its own label.

label: Raw shortcut
summary: Going by its name, the widget's keyboard shortcut as unformatted text.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it. Compare GetShortcut.

label: Mouse position (scaled)
summary: The mouse position over the widget as a pair of decimal numbers, scaled with the interface going by its name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type directly; the royal court window positions an element at AccessParent.GetScaledMousePosition, which fits the name. Compare GetUnscaledMousePositionInteger.

label: Shortcut
summary: Going by its name, the widget's keyboard shortcut as text.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it. Compare GetRawShortcut.

label: Tooltip lock progress
summary: How far a tooltip is on its way to being locked, as a decimal number from 0 to 1.
details: Vanilla feeds it into small progress bars (min 0, max 1) in the tooltip layouts, shown while the tooltip is not yet locked and the layout uses timer locking.

label: Mouse position (unscaled)
summary: The mouse position over the widget as a pair of whole numbers, not scaled with the interface going by its name.
details: Vanilla passes it to the royal court window's hover, click and right-click handlers, so the 3D court scene knows where the player points.

label: Video control
summary: The widget seen as a video control (an element that plays a video), going by its name and return type.
details: It is a promote: it leads on to a PdxGuiGfxVideoControl object whose own functions can follow. Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Hide widget
summary: An action that hides the interface widget.
details: Vanilla calls it from an animation state of the activity pulse popup, which hides itself 5 seconds after it appears. It returns nothing. Compare Show.

label: Stop animation
summary: An action that stops a running animation of the widget, named by its state.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla calls it in the bookmark screen with the state 'bookmark_group_reset'. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the animation state to stop.
fields.values: a state name in quotes, for example 'bookmark_group_reset'

label: Restart animation
summary: An action that stops one animation of the widget and then starts another, going by its name.
details: It takes two state names, going by the name first the one to stop and then the one to start. Vanilla never uses it; it returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the name, the animation state to stop.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Going by the name, the animation state to start.

label: Is nested tooltip
summary: Yes or no: whether the tooltip is one opened from inside another tooltip, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visible check of an invisible button in the tooltip layout that closes all tooltips when clicked.

label: Is tooltip locked
summary: Yes or no: whether the tooltip is locked (the game's own state; the input does not say more).
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip layout to show some parts only once the tooltip is locked, and to show the lock progress circle while it is not yet locked (together with UsesTimerLocking). What locking means for the player is not documented.

label: Decision with parameter
summary: A decision prepared with one value handed to it, for use as a widget's data context.
details: Going by its name and its use. Vanilla uses it in the faith and holy site windows as a data context: it passes a decision key ('elevate_holy_site_decision', 'pam_extract_relic_decision' ...), the text 'selected_item' and a scope made from the holy site or the character (MakeScope). What the game does with them is not documented; likely the decision is prepared for that holy site or character. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the decision.
fields.values: a decision key in quotes, for example 'elevate_holy_site_decision'

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A name for the value handed over (not documented); vanilla always writes 'selected_item'.
fields.values: a name in quotes, in vanilla 'selected_item'

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The value handed over.
fields.values: a scope made with MakeScope, for example HolySite.MakeScope or Character.MakeScope

label: Widget itself
summary: The current interface widget itself.
details: Vanilla passes it to functions that need the widget, for example PdxGetWidgetScreenSize(PdxGuiWidget.Self) when asking for a portrait for the bookmark screen and the credits. The game documents no return type.

label: Show widget
summary: An action that makes the interface widget visible.
details: Vanilla calls it from an animation state of the activity pulse popup when a new pulse action appears. It returns nothing. Compare Hide.

label: Move to back
summary: An action that moves the widget behind its siblings, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it returns nothing. Compare StackTop.

label: Move to front
summary: An action that brings the widget in front of its siblings, going by its name.
details: Vanilla calls it once, when the barbershop window's show animation starts. It returns nothing.

label: Start animation
summary: An action that starts one of the widget's animation states, named by its state.
details: Vanilla calls it when tabs are created in the character and realm windows ('tab_active'), and after FindChild in the bookmark screen. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the animation state to start.
fields.values: a state name in quotes, for example 'tab_active'

label: Access setting itself
summary: A function on a setting (one option in the game's settings menu) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf in the activity windows is a different type and only a hint.

label: Access setting
summary: A function on a setting entry of the settings menu that gives access to the setting, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the settings layout passes EnumSettingEntry.AccessSetting when an option of a choice setting is clicked, which is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Has unsaved changes
summary: Yes or no: whether the setting was changed without being saved yet, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Setting
summary: The setting behind a row of the settings menu, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla's settings layout hands it to PdxValueSetting.GetValue (as a value), PdxValueSetting.GetFormatedValue (as a text) and GetIsChecked (as a checked state). The game documents no return type.

label: Core setting
summary: The setting seen as a core setting object, whose own functions can follow.
details: It is a promote leading to a PdxCoreSetting. Vanilla uses GetSettingPromoted.RequireRestart together with JominiGUISetting.ShouldShow in a visible check, likely for a note on settings that need a restart.

label: Setting name
summary: The shown name of a setting in the settings menu, as text.
details: Vanilla's settings layout shows it as the label of each setting row.

label: Setting tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a setting in the settings menu.
details: Vanilla's settings layout uses it as the tooltip of setting rows.

label: Setting itself
summary: A function on a setting of the settings menu that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type; lines with Self on other types, such as Character.Self, are only a hint.

label: Access settings window
summary: A function on the settings window that hands back the window object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Can apply
summary: Yes or no: whether the settings window allows applying the changes, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Can restore
summary: Yes or no: whether the settings window allows restoring settings, going by its name (likely to their defaults).
details: Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Applies on restart
summary: Yes or no: whether the changed settings only take effect after a restart, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Has changed
summary: Yes or no: whether something was changed in the settings window, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; its settings layout uses JominiSettingsWindow.HasChanged instead, a different type and only a hint.

label: Apply settings
summary: An action of the settings window that applies the changes, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it returns nothing.

label: Cancel settings
summary: An action of the settings window that cancels the changes, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it returns nothing.

label: Restore settings
summary: An action of the settings window that restores settings, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it returns nothing.

label: Save settings
summary: An action of the settings window that saves the settings, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it returns nothing.

label: Settings window itself
summary: A function on the settings window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access settings category
summary: A function on a category of the settings window (a group of settings) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Category name
summary: The name of a settings category, as text, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetName lines on other types, such as traits, are only a hint.

label: Settings category itself
summary: A function on a settings category that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access value setting
summary: A function on a value setting (a setting set by a number, such as a slider) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Shown setting value
summary: The current value of a number setting, written out as text for display.
details: It takes the setting. Vanilla's settings layout uses it as a text, passing PdxSetting.GetSetting. The game spells the name with one t (Formated).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The setting whose value to show.

label: Setting value
summary: The current value of a number setting, as a decimal number.
details: It takes the setting. Vanilla's settings layout uses it as the value of an element, passing PdxSetting.GetSetting, likely a slider.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The setting whose value to read.

label: Value setting itself
summary: A function on a value setting that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access perk itself
summary: A function on a perk (something unlocked in the lifestyle window) that hands back the perk itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Perk blockers
summary: Text listing what keeps a perk from being taken, going by its name.
details: It takes one argument, going by similar functions likely the character. Vanilla never names it on this type; the culture window's AddTraditionWindow.GetBlockers is a different type and only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by similar functions, the character checked.

label: Perk effects
summary: Text describing what a perk does for the given character.
details: Vanilla shows it in the perk tooltip of the lifestyle window under the perk's name, passing the character shown, and in the shared tooltip with the player.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the effects are described for.
fields.values: a character, for example Character.Self or GetPlayer

label: Perk icon
summary: The perk's icon picture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of perk icons in the lifestyle window's perk trees. The game documents no return type.

label: Perk's lifestyle
summary: The lifestyle the perk belongs to.
details: The lifestyle window uses it to name that lifestyle in a warning that no perk unlock is available in it. The game documents no return type, but vanilla takes the lifestyle's name from the result.

label: Perk name
summary: The perk's name as text, for a given character.
details: Effect texts use it to say which perk a character gains or loses ("loses the ... Perk"), always passing that character. Why the name depends on a character is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the name is shown for; vanilla passes the character who gains or loses the perk.

label: Perk name, no tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the perk's name as text without a tooltip, for the given character.
details: It takes a character. Vanilla shows it as the title of the perk tooltip and as text in the lifestyle window, passing the character shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the name is shown for.

label: Unlocked trait
summary: The trait that taking the perk gives, going by its name and its use.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of a trait shown in the lifestyle window. The game documents no return type.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the perk has an icon, going by its name.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type; HasIcon on laws and game concepts in tooltips is only a hint.

label: Unlocks a trait
summary: Yes or no: whether taking the perk gives a trait, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. Compare GetUnlockTrait.

label: Is final perk
summary: Yes or no: whether the perk is a "finisher", going by its name the last perk of its tree.
details: Going by its name and its use: the lifestyle window shows different parts for finisher perks than for the others, and a separate one for a finisher when no trait is valid.

label: Perk itself
summary: The perk itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it in the lifestyle window, for example to Character.HasPerk( Perk.Self ), CharacterLifestyleWindow.CanSelectPerkDesc and PerkGuiTree.GetItemPosition. The game documents no return type.

label: Access perk tree itself
summary: A function on a perk tree of the lifestyle window that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Perk tree background
summary: The background picture of a perk tree in the lifestyle window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the lifestyle window, likely behind a perk tree. The game documents no return type.

label: Perk tree lines
summary: The list of connections between perks in a perk tree, used to draw the lines between them.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla uses it as a list source in the lifestyle window; each item is a PerkLineConnection with line start and end points.

label: Perk position
summary: Where a perk sits in the perk tree drawing, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: It takes the perk. Vanilla uses it to place each perk icon in the lifestyle window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The perk to place.

label: Perks in tree
summary: The list of perks in a perk tree.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla uses it as the list source of the perk icons of a tree in the lifestyle window. The game documents no return type.

label: Perk tree name
summary: The name of a perk tree, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the lifestyle window.

label: Has unlocked perk
summary: Yes or no: whether the given perk of the tree is already unlocked.
details: It takes the perk. Vanilla uses it in visible checks of the lifestyle window's perk lines, alone and combined with CharacterLifestyleWindow.CanSelectPerkIgnoreCost, so different line parts show depending on whether the perk is unlocked or can be taken.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The perk to check.

label: Is tree completed
summary: Yes or no: whether every perk of the tree is taken, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the lifestyle window only while the tree is not completed.

label: Perk tree itself
summary: A function on a perk tree that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Set up line area
summary: Prepares the given widget as the area the perk tree's lines are drawn in, going by its name; returns yes or no.
details: Vanilla calls it from the visible check of a widget in the lifestyle window, passing the widget itself (PdxGuiWidget.Self); likely the setup runs when the widget is evaluated.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget to set up.

label: Access perk line itself
summary: A function on a line between two perks in a perk tree that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Lower end of perk line
summary: The perk entry a perk tree line leads to (the later perk), going by its name.
details: Vanilla follows it with GetItem to reach the perk, then checks whether that perk is unlocked or can be taken. The game documents no return type. Compare GetParent.

label: Line start point
summary: Where a line between two perks starts, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the from point of the lines drawn in the lifestyle window's perk trees.

label: Line end point
summary: Where a line between two perks ends, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the to point of the lines drawn in the lifestyle window's perk trees.

label: Upper end of perk line
summary: The perk entry a perk tree line comes from (the earlier perk), going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the game documents no return type. Compare GetChild.

label: Perk line itself
summary: A function on a perk tree line that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access perk entry itself
summary: A function on a perk entry at the end of a perk tree line that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Perk of entry
summary: The perk that a perk tree entry stands for.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla sets it as a data context in the lifestyle window and checks it after PerkLineConnection.GetChild. The game documents no return type.

label: Perk entry itself
summary: A function on a perk tree entry that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Set up bottom widget
summary: Going by its name, sets up the given widget for the bottom of a perk entry; returns yes or no.
details: Vanilla calls it from a visible check in the lifestyle window, passing the widget itself. Compare SetupTopWidget.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget to set up.

label: Set up top widget
summary: Going by its name, sets up the given widget for the top of a perk entry; returns yes or no.
details: Vanilla calls it from a visible check in the lifestyle window, passing the widget itself. Compare SetupBottomWidget.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget to set up.

label: Access beliefs window
summary: A function on the personal beliefs window (a character's own tenets and spiritual fulfillment) that hands back the window itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Close beliefs window
summary: An action that closes the personal beliefs window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the window's close button. It returns nothing.

label: Character
summary: The character whose personal beliefs the window shows.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context and shows its personal tenet slot breakdown as a tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Fulfillment bar
summary: The data behind a multi-part bar in the personal beliefs window, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the window; going by the window, likely the spiritual fulfillment meter. The game documents no return type.

label: Spiritual fulfillment
summary: The character's current spiritual fulfillment, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the fulfillment level and as the value of the fulfillment meter in the personal beliefs window.

label: Doctrines
summary: The list of doctrines shown in the personal beliefs window.
details: Going by its name and its use as a list source in the window (it has a doctrines tab). The game documents no return type.

label: Fulfillment breakdown
summary: Text breaking down a spiritual fulfillment value into its parts, going by its name.
details: It takes one argument that the game does not document. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented.

label: Icon
summary: An icon picture of the personal beliefs window, picked by one argument, going by its name.
details: The game documents neither the argument nor the return type, and vanilla never names it on this type; GetIcon on other types is only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented.

label: Personal tenets
summary: The list of the character's personal tenets (tenets they hold for themselves).
details: Going by its name and its use as a list source in the personal beliefs window. The game documents no return type.

label: Personal tenets heading
summary: The heading text above the personal tenets in the personal beliefs window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the window.

label: Rite
summary: The rite shown in the personal beliefs window, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the window. Character.GetRite is passed when tenets are named in the fulfillment change breakdown, but that is another type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Tenet being replaced
summary: The personal tenet the player chose to replace while picking its replacement.
details: Vanilla names it in the picking header (Choose a personal tenet to replace …) and in the fulfillment change breakdown, and compares it with each tenet to mark the one being swapped.

label: Tenet groups
summary: The list of tenet groups shown when picking a personal tenet, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list source in the personal beliefs window. The game documents no return type.

label: Tenet sorting
summary: The object that sorts the tenets in the personal beliefs window, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the window. The game documents no return type.

label: Is active level
summary: Yes or no: whether a given level is the active one, going by its name (likely a spiritual fulfillment level).
details: It takes one argument the game does not document. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by the name, the level checked.

label: Is active tab
summary: Yes or no: whether the named tab of the personal beliefs window is the one shown.
details: Vanilla uses it to show tab buttons as pressed, for example IsActiveTab( 'tab_tenets' ). Compare SetActiveTab.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the tab.
fields.values: a tab name in quotes, for example 'tab_tenets' or 'tab_doctrines'

label: Is adding tenet
summary: Yes or no: whether the player is picking a new personal tenet to add.
details: Vanilla shows the tenet picking view while this or IsSwappingPersonalTenet is true, and the normal view otherwise.

label: Is replacing tenet
summary: Yes or no: whether the player is picking a tenet to replace one of their personal tenets.
details: Vanilla shows the tenet picking view while this or IsAddingPersonalTenet is true, and the normal view otherwise.

label: Remove personal tenet
summary: An action that removes the given personal tenet from the character.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button on each personal tenet, passing that tenet. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tenet to remove.

label: Pick personal tenet
summary: An action that picks the given tenet as the new personal tenet (added, or replacing the one being swapped).
details: Vanilla calls it from the buttons of the tenet list in picking mode. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tenet chosen.

label: Beliefs window itself
summary: A function on the personal beliefs window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Switch tab
summary: An action that switches the personal beliefs window to the named tab.
details: Vanilla calls it from the tab buttons ('tab_tenets', 'tab_doctrines') and when the window opens, to start on the tenets tab. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the tab to show.
fields.values: a tab name in quotes, for example 'tab_tenets'

label: Start adding tenet
summary: An action that opens the picking of a new personal tenet to add.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button in the personal beliefs window. It returns nothing.

label: Start replacing tenet
summary: An action that opens the picking of a tenet to replace the given personal tenet.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button on a personal tenet, passing that tenet. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tenet to replace.

label: Stop picking tenet
summary: An action that leaves the tenet picking view without choosing.
details: Vanilla calls it from buttons of the personal beliefs window. It returns nothing.

label: Access rally point tool
summary: A function on the rally point placing tool that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Close rally point window
summary: An action that closes the rally point window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button in the rally point window. It returns nothing.

label: Is moving rally point
summary: Yes or no: whether the player is moving an existing rally point, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a visible check in the rally point window.

label: Is placing rally point
summary: Yes or no: whether the player is placing a new rally point, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a visible check in the rally point window.

label: Rally point tool itself
summary: A function on the rally point placing tool that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access project planning
summary: A function on the great project planning window that hands back the window itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Can open planning map
summary: Yes or no: whether the map mode for choosing the project's place can be opened.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the button that opens that map mode, and shows the reason from GetCannotOpenPlanMapModeReason as a tooltip when it is false.

label: Close project planning
summary: An action that closes the great project planning window.
details: Vanilla calls it from buttons in the window. It returns nothing.

label: Why map can't open
summary: Text telling why the map mode for choosing the project's place cannot be opened.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the great project planning window. Compare CanOpenPlanMapMode.

label: Expected end date
summary: The date the planned great project is expected to be finished.
details: Vanilla shows how long from now that is (Expected to be finished in …) and checks whether it lies after today. The game documents no return type.

label: Required contributions
summary: The list of contributions the planned great project must get.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla shows it as a list in the planning window and checks whether it is empty. The game documents no return type.

label: Optional contributions
summary: The list of contributions the planned great project may get but does not need.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla shows it as a list in the planning window and checks whether it is empty. The game documents no return type.

label: Planner
summary: The character planning the great project.
details: Vanilla passes it to GreatProjectType.SatisfiesRequirements and GetIllustration in the planning window. The game documents no return type.

label: Project type
summary: The type of great project being planned.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the planning window. The game documents no return type.

label: Chosen province
summary: The province chosen as the place of the planned great project.
details: Vanilla shows its name (In …), sets it as a data context and checks the project's requirements against it. The game documents no return type.

label: Project planning itself
summary: A function on the great project planning window that hands back the window itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Open planning map
summary: An action that opens the map mode for choosing where to build the great project.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button in the planning window. It returns nothing.

label: Access planned phase
summary: A planned activity phase (one step of an activity being planned) itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the activity planner's actions, for example to remove a phase, choose its type or move it earlier. The game documents no return type.

label: Guest position in group
summary: The position of a character within a guest group of the phase, as a whole number, going by its name.
details: It takes two arguments the game does not document; going by IsCharacterInGuestSubset, likely the character and the group name. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by similar functions, the character.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Not documented; going by similar functions, the guest group name.

label: Phase location
summary: The location where the planned activity phase takes place.
details: Vanilla shows its name as the travel plan destination (when HasLocation is true) and reaches the holder of its title in the activity planner. The game documents no return type, so what kind of object it is (likely a province) is not documented.

label: Phase type
summary: The kind of phase this planned activity step is, for example a tournament contest.
details: Vanilla shows its name in tournament texts (You participated in the …). The game documents no return type.

label: Has location
summary: Yes or no: whether the planned activity phase has a location chosen.
details: Vanilla's travel plan shows the location's name when true, and Choose a location otherwise.

label: Has phase type
summary: Yes or no: whether a phase type is set for this planned step, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a visible check in the tournament contest selection.

label: Is in guest group
summary: Yes or no: whether the given character belongs to the named guest group of the phase.
details: Vanilla checks, for example, whether the player is in the 'contestant' group to word tournament participation texts.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character to check.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The name of the guest group.
fields.values: a group name in quotes, for example 'contestant'

label: Is predefined
summary: Yes or no: whether the phase is predefined (set by the activity, not chosen), going by its name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; a debug window uses IsPredefined on another type, only a hint.

label: Planned phase itself
summary: The planned activity phase itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it, for example, to ActivityLocaleWindow.GetGuestSublist in tournament result texts. The game documents no return type.

label: Access playable
summary: A function on a playable entry that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Character
summary: The character of a playable entry in the game's lobby, that is the character a player would play.
details: The multiplayer lobby reaches it from a lobby player to show that player's character name, and the ruler designer from the selected playable to show the character's camp or estate location. The game documents no return type, but vanilla uses the result as a character.

label: Playable itself
summary: A function on a playable entry that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Accept join request
summary: An action that lets a player who asked to join the multiplayer game in.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button of the multiplayer join request. It returns nothing. Compare Reject.

label: Access join request
summary: A function on a multiplayer join request that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Player name
summary: The name of the player asking to join the multiplayer game, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the join request.

label: Reject join request
summary: An action that turns away a player who asked to join the multiplayer game.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button of the multiplayer join request. It returns nothing. Compare Accept.

label: Join request itself
summary: A function on a multiplayer join request that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access message
summary: A function on a player message (a notification shown to the player) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Arrival date
summary: The game date the message reached the player, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it as a date in notifications, the message popup and the message settings window. The game documents no return type. Compare GetDate.

label: Merged message count
summary: How many messages were merged into this one, as a whole number, going by its name.
details: Vanilla subtracts 2 from it for the number shown in the "others" text of merged messages (message_consolidation_others).

label: Merged message names
summary: Text listing the names from the messages merged into this one, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it in the Others tooltip of merged messages.

label: Message date
summary: The date of the message.
details: Vanilla shows it as a short date without the year in the message popup. The game documents no return type. Compare GetArrivalDate.

label: Message text
summary: The description text of the message.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text and tooltip of notifications.

label: Left artifact
summary: An artifact the message is about, the one in its left slot, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in notifications and names it in artifact messages (You acquired … and …) next to GetRightArtifact. The game documents no return type.

label: Left character
summary: A character the message is about, the one in its left slot, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in notifications and the message popup, likely to show a portrait. The game documents no return type.

label: Left doctrine
summary: A doctrine the message is about, the one in its left slot, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in notifications and the message popup. The game documents no return type.

label: Left dynasty
summary: A dynasty the message is about, the one in its left slot, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in notifications and the message popup. The game documents no return type.

label: Left faith
summary: A faith the message is about, the one in its left slot, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in notifications and the message popup. The game documents no return type.

label: Left house
summary: A house (dynasty branch) the message is about, the one in its left slot, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in notifications and the message popup. The game documents no return type.
